Paragraph:
Translation: The great generals who have highly esteemed your name and fame will think that you have left the battlefield out of fear only, and thus they will consider you a coward.

Purport (Excerpt): Do not think that the great generals like Duryodhana, Karna, and other contemporaries will think that you have left the battlefield out of compassion for your brothers and grandfather. They will think that you have left out of fear for your life. And thus their high estimation of your personality will go to hell.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna is rationalizing his desire to flee by framing it as a noble act of 'compassion' and expects others to recognize his moral high ground.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna ruthlessly reality-tests Arjuna's rationalization. He points out that Arjuna's peers and enemies will not perceive his actions as compassionate; they will objectively view his retreat as pure fear and cowardice.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna's delusion of a 'noble retreat' is shattered, forcing him to view his actions through the realistic lens of his society.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Reality Testing: Checking one's internal beliefs against external facts
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Perspective Taking: Understanding how others will truly perceive an action

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Bhaya (Fear, the actual root cause of Arjuna's desire to flee, disguised as compassion)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The world judges actions based on one's prescribed duties. If a warrior leaves a battlefield, it is universally condemned as fear, regardless of the internal sentimental justifications (like misplaced compassion) the warrior might try to use.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is a masterclass in breaking down 'rationalization.' Arjuna has built an elaborate, noble-sounding excuse (compassion for family) to avoid a terrifying situation. Krishna strips away this defense mechanism by forcing Arjuna to see the situation from the outside. By exposing the underlying fear behind the 'compassion,' Krishna compels Arjuna to face his true motives.
